title: Marcos says playing of Pinoy hit song 'Anak' in China a 'terrific' choice
summary: President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Friday shrugged off speculations about the playing of the hit song, "Anak", when he was welcomed in the gala dinner of the 2026 Asia Pacific Economic…

blocks.text: SHENZHEN, China — President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. on Friday shrugged off speculations about the playing of the hit song, "Anak", when he was welcomed in the gala dinner of the 2026 Asia Pacific Economic Conference (APEC) summit in China.

In a kapihan with the media, the President said he was surprised when "Anak" was played when he was welcomed during the gala dinner, emphasizing that the song is the "biggest international Filipino hit" that the Philippines has.
"Wasn’t it terrific? I think it was great," Marcos told reporters.
"Their choice of that song was a very, very warm gesture. It makes you feel at home," he added.
According to the President, Filipino folk song "Leron, Leron Sinta" was also played during the gala dinner proper.
An orchestra in Shenzhen, China played an instrumental version of "Anak" when Marcos and First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos entered a hall in Shenzhen on Wednesday for a gala dinner with fellow leaders.

Released in 1978, "Anak" was written and performed by the late folk singer-songwriter Freddie Aguilar. It is regarded as one of the most successful Original Pilipino Music (OPM) singles of all time, spawning translated versions in various languages.
"Anak" tells the story of a child who refused the advice of his or her parents, fell into bad vices, and regretted his rebellious past.
On Thursday, Malacañang downplayed the song choice for Marcos' entrance, saying that "Anak" is a "classic" and was a global hit. — VDV, GMA News
